persona.bio: Dani, 34, runs a mobile dog grooming van on her own in a suburb of Atlanta. Six or seven dogs a day. Clients book by text, and she answers the same questions all day: prices by breed, how long it takes, whether she does nails only, how to reschedule. She sends reminder texts the night before, writes a short note after each groom about matting or skin, and posts before and after photos on Instagram. Bookings live in a paper diary and her phone's calendar. She has never used AI.

steps.firstStep: I’m a mobile dog groomer who runs my own grooming van, and I answer owner text messages many times a day. Write a short, friendly text reply to the message I paste below. Keep it under 60 words, warm and plain, with no emojis. Only say what I’ve told you. If the owner asks about a time, price or service I haven’t given, say I’ll check and get back to them. Here is the owner’s message: [paste the owner’s message here]

steps.note: I run my own mobile dog grooming van. I book appointments, text owners, groom dogs and post on Instagram, all from my phone. I write to dog owners, and sometimes to people who follow my page. My tone is warm, friendly and short, like a quick text from someone who loves their dogs. I like replies of one to three sentences, in plain words. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, times, openings or promises about a dog’s coat or health. If something is missing, put it in square brackets so I can fill it in. Never use fancy words. Always give me something I can read and send as it is.

steps.title: Answering owner messages, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each a few letters away. You type a short shortcut and the whole reply is one tap from going in. Owners get a quick answer in your own words, and you stop typing the same price and timing answers from scratch.

material.label: Your replies
items: Hi [first name], thanks for reaching out! Let me check my calendar and I’ll get right back to you with a time.
Hi [first name], yes, your appointment is still on for [day and time]. See you and [dog’s name] then!
Hi [first name], I can do a nails only visit for [dog’s name]. Just let me know what day works and I’ll check my calendar.
Hi [first name], my prices depend on the size and coat of your dog. Can you tell me the breed and how long it’s been since the last groom? Then I’ll send you a price and the time it takes.
Hi [first name], a friendly reminder that [dog’s name] has an appointment on [day and time]. Please text me if anything changes!
Hi [first name], I’m on my way and will be there around [time]. See you soon!
Hi [first name], thank you for having me today! [dog’s name] was a joy. Let me know when you’d like to book the next visit.

steps.title: Your Instagram posts, said out loud, finished as text
steps.read: You say your post out loud, and Claude turns it into finished text that waits for your OK. You skip the blank page and keep your own voice. You read it, change what you want, then post it yourself.

material.label: Instructions for your assistant
items: I run my own mobile dog grooming van and I post on Instagram. I will tell you out loud what I want to post about, like a groom I just finished, an opening in my schedule or a tip for dog owners. Turn what I say into a finished Instagram caption in my voice, which is warm, friendly and short, in two to four sentences. Use only the details I give you. Do not add prices, times, offers or claims about a dog’s health or coat that I did not say. Do not use the dog owner’s name or any private details. If something is missing, put it in square brackets so I can fill it in. Give me the caption first, then a short line of hashtag ideas I can choose from.

material.label: What to say each time
items: What the post is about, like a before and after, a tip or an opening in my schedule
The dog’s breed or size, only if I want it in the post
Anything I want said, like a date, a time or how to book
Anything to leave out
The feeling I want, like fun, calm or proud
Whether I want hashtags

safeUse: Never type an owner’s full name, phone number or home address into Claude. Use square brackets or just say “an owner”.
Never type a dog’s health or medical details tied to a person, like a vet record or medication notes.
Keep prices, times and openings out of what you ask Claude to invent. Add the real ones yourself.
Read every reply and every post before it goes out, and fix anything that does not sound like you.
For any health question about a dog, send the owner to their vet instead of using a draft.

design.today: You answer owner texts many times a day, one by one. You text back right away, check the calendar first, or look up your notes.
design.newWay: Your most common replies, like price, timing and whether a Tuesday slot still works, are saved on your phone so each one is a few letters away. You still check Google Calendar for the actual slot and read each reply before you send it. Answers stay the same every time, and you stop retyping what you have already said a hundred times.

steps.goal: Pick your ten most common owner questions, such as price, timing, nails only and sore dogs, and write down your usual answer to each.
Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so you have a helper to tidy your replies.
Turn your ten answers into short saved replies on your phone keyboard, each a few letters away.
Keep checking the calendar yourself for open slots and fill the day and time into the saved reply before sending.

material.label: Saved replies
material.what: Ten short replies for your most common owner questions, written in your own voice with gaps for the day and time.

material.label: Shortcut list
material.what: A list of the few letters that bring up each saved reply, so you can find them quickly.

material.label: Tricky case notes
material.what: A short note on how you answer questions like a sore dog or nails only, so those replies stay kind and consistent.

design.checkPoint: You read every reply and check the day and time against your calendar before you send it.

design.today: You write social posts now and then, each one from a blank page.
design.newWay: You keep one saved assistant that knows your voice and your van. After a groom, you tell it in a few words about the dog and what you did, and it gives you a caption to start from. You change anything that is off and post it yourself, so each post starts from something instead of a blank page.

steps.goal: Get Claude ready on your phone so you have a place to ask for post drafts.
Make a project for your social posts so your tone notes and examples stay in one place.
Set up a saved assistant that turns a few words about a groom into a caption in your voice.
Paste the caption you approve into Instagram and post it yourself.

material.label: Assistant instructions
material.what: Plain instructions telling the assistant to write short, friendly captions for a mobile dog grooming van.

material.label: Tone notes
material.what: A few lines on how you sound, such as warm and playful, and words you like or avoid.

material.label: Post starter
material.what: A short fill in form for the dog's breed, the groom you did and anything fun, so each draft starts quickly.

design.checkPoint: You read each caption and check the dog's name and details before you post it yourself, and only post photos of dogs whose owners are happy to be shown.
